transcript: On a painfully hot and humid Friday night, I made my way down to The Little Island to catch The Gospel at Colonus, and it was so worth bearing the heat. This musical isn't new, but it was new to me. Based on the Sophocles play Oedipus at Colonus, The Gospel at Colonus translates this portion of the Oedipus Cycle from a Greek tragedy to a religious parable. Recontextualized as a Black church service, we have a preacher/narrator, principal singers embodying the primary characters in the story, and a gospel choir functioning as the Greek chorus. This is a concept that I would have never thought to explore for this story, but the themes of fate, forgiveness, and redemption actually make it very well-suited for a religious service. I think being familiar with the Oedipus Cycle was helpful here, but you could come into this piece anywhere along the spectrum of familiarity and still get a lot out of it. I thought the storytelling here was strong, but if nothing else, this production was fantastically directed and performed. The musical direction and the vocal performances alone were well worth the price of admission, and having snagged a rush ticket, I was actually astounded by the experience that was afforded to me for only $15. This production closed over the weekend, but it's worth keeping an eye out for future productions at The Amph on The Little Island which is not only a really beautiful performance space, but one that tends to host various kinds of live performances at very affordable prices.
